idea-plugin.name: Yamlix - Ansible Variable Resolution
idea-plugin.description:
Which value does this variable actually have — on which host, and why?

A variable in Ansible does not have a definition. It has as many as the precedence table allows, and which one wins depends on the host, the inventory, and where in the play you are. Yamlix models that properly.

  • Ansible tool window — every variable the open file uses and defines, its effective value, which playbooks reach the file and which hosts that means. Select a variable to see every definition site with the inventories and groups it holds on.
  • Ctrl/⌘+Click on {{ a_variable }} lists every definition site, ordered by what applies at the caret — not a name-based list that reads the same everywhere.
  • Quick Documentation shows the effective value per inventory and host, with hosts that agree collapsed and hosts that differ kept apart.
  • Navigation for roles, include_role, include_tasks, vars_files, include_vars, template/copy sources, notify handlers, and hosts: patterns into INI and YAML inventories.
  • Find Usages from a definition to every use, including through include_tasks.

It never guesses. Anything Ansible can only know at run time is rendered as unresolved with the raw template shown: a fact-templated include_vars lists every candidate and promotes none; register, hostvars, lookup() and vault are named explicitly. There is deliberately no code path that invents a value.

The precedence rules were verified by running ansible-playbook and ansible-inventory against a fixture project with ansible-core 2.20.4 — not reasoned from the documentation. Two fixture projects serve as the executable specification, and a test asserts the code cannot drift from them.

Reuses the platform's YAML PSI. Registers no file type, does not claim *.yml, and never shells out to ansible. Ansible context is detected structurally, per file.

idea-plugin.change-notes:
See the changelog for the full history.

  • New Ansible tool window: the variables of the file you are reading, their effective values, and where each one comes from.
  • Variable resolution roughly twenty times faster on fleet-sized projects.
  • A hosts: pattern that cannot be evaluated no longer makes a role's variables resolve to nothing.
  • group_vars/host_vars beside the playbook are recognised and correctly outrank the inventory's own.
  • Playbooks are found anywhere under the ansible.cfg directory.
